31 In an electrolyte, the electric current is carried by charged particles (ions) in solution.
What is not a possible value for the charge on an ion in solution?
C
A
– 4.8 × 10–19
B
+1.6 × 10–19
C
C
+3.2 × 10–19
C
D
+4.0 × 10–19
C

hints: Notice all four charges are a few times $10^{-19} \text{ C}$ - recall the magnitude of the elementary charge $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
Use charge quantisation for ions: any ion charge must satisfy $Q = ne$ where $n$ is a positive or negative whole number.
Divide each listed charge in $\text{C}$ by $1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and check which division does not give a whole number for $n$.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: charge is quantised, so an ion in solution must have charge $Q = ne$, where $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and $n = \pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 3...$.
Check option A: $n = -4.8 \times 10^{-19} / 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = -3$, a whole number, so possible.
Check option B: $n = +1.6 \times 10^{-19} / 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = +1$, a whole number, so possible.
Check option C: $n = +3.2 \times 10^{-19} / 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = +2$, a whole number, so possible.
Check option D: $n = +4.0 \times 10^{-19} / 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = +2.5$, which is not a whole number and would require half an electron, so it is not possible. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is $-3 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, a loss or gain of 3 whole electrons, so it is a possible ion charge.

B.explanation: This is $+1 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, the charge of one missing electron, so it is a possible ion charge.

C.explanation: This is $+2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, the charge of two missing electrons, so it is a possible ion charge.

D.explanation: This is $2.5 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, which is not a whole number of elementary charges, so it cannot occur.
